question: Can a fully logged, rerunnable pipeline with a pinned software version reproduce, from the public rdrobust_senate file, the printed default output of Calonico, Cattaneo, Farrell and Titiunik (2017, Sec. 7.2) for the US Senate incumbency advantage (conventional local-linear estimate and robust bias-corrected 95% CI), and how far do the estimate and its falsification checks move across the bandwidth and software choices that the published output leaves open? This is a replication: the estimate and the standard falsification checks on these data are already published (CCFT 2017; Cattaneo, Frandsen and Titiunik 2015), and the paper claims no new finding about the incumbency advantage.
hypotheses: H1 (computational reproduction; targets are the printed values verified by the Scout: conventional estimate 7.416, robust bias-corrected 95% CI [4.094, 10.926], N = 1,297 with h = 17.708): with the rdrobust version pinned in code/requirements.txt and the published defaults (p = 1, triangular kernel, mserd bandwidth, NN variance), each target is reproduced if |replicated - published| <= 0.01 percentage points; N must match exactly. Because H1 holds by construction if the software is deterministic and the version matches, a pass is reported as a computational check, not as evidence about the incumbency advantage. A failure is diagnosed (version, platform), not tuned away.

H2 (falsification; tests fixed in design.method, each family Holm-adjusted on its own, no cross-family conclusion): (a) density test of margin at 0 with rddensity on all 1,390 margins, robust bias-corrected T_Q and its p-value, MDE fixed in run design-mde; (b) each of the four seed covariates (class and population N = 1,390; termshouse and termssenate N = 1,108) as the outcome of the H1 rdrobust specification, robust p-values Holm-adjusted over the four at 5%, MDEs fixed in run design-mde; (c) placebo cutoffs at the median of margin on each side of 0, each estimated only on its own side, REPORT-ONLY: estimate, CI, N and bandwidth, with precision given by the CI width; no correction and no conclusion drawn from non-rejection; (d) selection on the outcome's missingness: rdrobust of vote_observed (1 if vote is non-missing) on margin with the H1 options, robust p-value; its MDE formula is fixed in design.method and its value is computed only in the post-gate run h2-selection. For (a), (b) and (d), non-rejection is reported as no evidence of a discontinuity larger than the stated MDE, not as proof of continuity. The (a) result and the (b) standard errors were seen at the design stage (see disclosures). These four covariates are a subset of the eight in Cattaneo, Frandsen and Titiunik (2015); their p-values are not compared one-to-one with that paper's.

H3 (descriptive sensitivity, no decision rule): the estimate and robust CI under the 2014 rdrobust bandwidths (h = 16.79369, b = 27.43745, as printed by CCFT 2017 and verified by the Scout), under half and double the H1 bandwidth h = 17.708, and with p = 2. Reported as a table; not used to change the H1 targets.
contribution: A logged, rerunnable replication of a standard regression-discontinuity estimate with the software version pinned and its falsification checks fixed before any outcome analysis, plus a descriptive account of how much the printed output depends on bandwidth and software defaults. No new claim about the incumbency advantage.

design.summary: A sharp regression-discontinuity replication of the US Senate incumbency advantage: local-linear rdrobust (p = 1, q = 2, triangular kernel, mserd bandwidth, NN variance, robust bias-corrected 95% CI) on the 1,297 elections with an observed outcome, run with rdrobust 2.1.1 (pinned). The primary H1 setting is masspoints = 'off', an assumption that the 2016 release used no mass-point adjustment; 'adjust' (the 2.1.1 default) is reported alongside it with the same tolerances. H1 targets are the printed conventional estimate 7.416, robust CI [4.09441, 10.9255], N = 1,297 and h = 17.708, checked to 0.01 pp and exact N. Falsification checks are fixed in advance and reported without a cross-family conclusion: a density test on margin (H2a), balance on the four seed covariates (H2b), one-sided placebo cutoffs reported as estimate and CI (H2c, report-only), and a selection test on vote_observed (H2d, run after the gate); H3 is descriptive sensitivity only.
design.method: H1 (main, run h1-rdrobust): rdrobust(y = vote, x = margin, c = 0, p = 1, q = 2, kernel = 'tri', bwselect = 'mserd', vce = 'nn', nnmatch = 3, level = 95), no covariates, so covs_drop is inert. Primary setting: masspoints = 'off'. Secondary setting, reported in the same run: masspoints = 'adjust' (the 2.1.1 default), with identical tolerances. Rows with missing vote (93) are dropped by rdrobust, giving N = 1,297 (595 left, 702 right). rd-effect = conventional estimate; rd-ci-low/high = robust bias-corrected CI. Assumption, not a sourced fact: that the 2016 release used no mass-point adjustment, so 'off' is the setting closest to its algorithm. No source in the workspace confirms this (sources/notes.md: the article prints only '2016 version'). The choice is not fixed by agreement with the printed numbers. What the option changes: under 'adjust' rdrobust 2.1.1 replaces the sample size in the bandwidth selector with M = M_l + M_r, the count of distinct margin values (1,352 in the full file against 1,390 rows; rdrobust.py line 721). This changes h even without a mass-point trigger. The bwcheck = 10 setting is applied under 'adjust' only when the share of mass points on a side reaches 20 percent (rdrobust.py lines 609-615). That condition is not met here: the mass points are the two values at -100 (2 observations, a mass share (1 minus unique values over rows) of about 0.002, i.e. 1 of 640 left-side rows) and the value at +100 (38 observations, a share of about 0.05 of the 750 right-side rows). So bwcheck is not triggered, and the only difference between the two settings is the M term. Tolerances (fixed now, same for both settings): |conventional - 7.416| <= 0.01 pp; each CI endpoint within 0.01 pp of 4.09441 and 10.9255; N exactly 1,297; |h - 17.708| <= 0.0005 (printed to 3 decimals). Decision rule: H1 is judged on the 'off' setting. A failure under 'off' is reported as a failure, with diagnosis (version, platform, option), and is not replaced by the 'adjust' result. The 'adjust' result is reported as a second reading and does not change the primary verdict. H2(a) density (run h2-density): rddensity(X = margin, c = 0, p = 2, kernel = 'triangular', vce = 'jackknife', bwselect = 'comb', massPoints = True, bino = default) on all 1,390 margins; primary statistic: robust bias-corrected test T_Q and its p-value; conventional T also reported. Why massPoints = True here but 'off' for rdrobust: the H1 'off' assumption concerns rdrobust's bandwidth selector (the M term, rdrobust.py line 721). rddensity has its own mass-point handling, and its default is massPoints = True; the H1 assumption does not transfer to it, so the density test keeps the package default and is not aligned to 'off'. What this changes: the margin's only ties are at +/-100, far outside the density bandwidth at 0, so the two settings are expected to give the same density test; this is an expectation, not a result. The h2-density run therefore also records p_Q under massPoints = False as a sensitivity metric (p_Q_nomass), reported next to p_Q with no decision rule. Margin is outcome-free, so this sample is fixed without reference to vote. Reported alone, with no correction across families. H2(b) covariates (run h2-covariates): for each of class, population (N = 1,390) and termshouse, termssenate (N = 1,108, complete cases), rdrobust(y = covariate, x = margin) with the H1 options at masspoints = 'off'; robust bias-corrected p-value per covariate, Holm-adjusted over the four at 5%. Holm applies within this family only. H2(c) placebo cutoffs (run h2-placebo): c_L = median of margin among margin < 0 and c_R = median of margin among margin > 0, both computed from margin only. Left test: rdrobust(y = vote, x = margin) on margin < 0 only, c = c_L; right test on margin > 0 only, c = c_R; H1 options at masspoints = 'off'. REPORT-ONLY: each placebo is reported as estimate, CI, p-value, N and bandwidth. No equivalence bound and no non-rejection claim are made. The precision is the CI width itself; the printed CFT 2015 Design II other-seat placebo CI [-2.69, 3.39] (about 6 pp wide) is a comparison of scale, not a bound. No multiplicity correction is applied to H2(c) because no conclusion is drawn from it. H2(d) selection (run h2-selection, run after the gate): rdrobust(y = vote_observed, x = margin) on all 1,390 rows, with the H1 options at masspoints = 'off'. vote_observed is 1 if vote is non-missing, a 0/1 indicator from the missingness pattern, not a statistic of vote's values. Primary statistic: robust bias-corrected p-value. Single test, no correction. Its MDE is fixed now as (z_0.975 + z_0.80) times its robust standard error, in percentage points of the share of observed outcomes; the value is computed only in run h2-selection after the gate. A discontinuity here would be a selection threat to H1 and is reported as such. Equivalence and power rules: H2(a): the minimum detectable difference in density at 0 (rddensity hat.diff scale, not a log ratio) is (z_0.975 + z_0.80) times the jackknife standard error under the null, computed from margin only in run design-mde. Values fixed now: MDE = 0.01136 density units (about 0.52 times the estimated left-side density 0.02169; the density difference is -0.00355, SE 0.00405). Disclosure: run design-mde also recorded the rddensity robust test on margin (T_Q = -0.875, p = 0.381), computed before the design gate. The h2-density run reproduces this specification, and this p-value is recorded here, not as a result. H2(b) MDE: (z_0.975 + z_0.80) times that test's robust standard error, computed in run design-mde (covariate-only). Values fixed now, in covariate units: class MDE 0.401 (N 1,390, robust SE 0.1431); termshouse MDE 1.400 (N 1,108, SE 0.4998); termssenate MDE 2.091 (N 1,108, SE 0.7462); population MDE 2,185,253 persons (N 1,390, SE 780,006). H2(c): no MDE and no equivalence bound (see report-only rule above). Placebo bandwidth cap rule (H2(c)): rdrobust 2.1.1 runs with bwrestrict = True (its default). Its cap on the bandwidth is c_bw = min(c_bw, bw_max), where bw_max = max(|c - x_min|, |c - x_max|) over the sample passed to the estimator (rdbwselect.py lines 651-655). The cap is therefore defined by the one-sided sample's x_min and x_max, not by |c|. For the left placebo (margin < 0), x_min is about -100 and x_max is the largest negative margin (about -0.08), so bw_max is about |c_L + 100|. For the right placebo (margin > 0), x_min is the smallest positive margin (about 0.04) and x_max is 100, so bw_max is about 100 - c_R. Each placebo run computes bw_max from its one-sided sample in the same way, and records bw_max, h, b, N_h left and right in its metrics. bw_capped = 1 when the final h or b equals bw_max (within 1e-9). A placebo with bw_capped = 1 is reported as boundary-limited; no statement is made beyond the report. H3 (descriptive, run h3-sensitivity, no decision rule): (i) printed 2014 bandwidths h = 16.79369, b = 27.43745, p = 1, masspoints 'off'; (ii) half of H1 bandwidths, h = 8.854, b = 13.992; (iii) double, h = 35.416, b = 55.968; (iv) p = 2, q = 3, mserd default bandwidth, masspoints 'off'; (v) H1 specification with masspoints = 'adjust'. Baseline for (ii) and (iii) is h = 17.708, b = 27.984. Software: code/requirements.txt pins rdrobust==2.1.1 and rddensity==3.0. Any run that is not one of the listed runs is out of design.
design.data: Source: rdrobust_senate.csv from rdpackages/rdrobust commit 2589686d (sha256 def1fc6b...2ad44; data/manifest.json senate-rd; no licence stated). Unit: a US Senate election, 1914 to 2010, 1,390 rows, 50 states. Running variable margin: Democratic margin of victory at t, percentage points, cutoff 0 (640 negative, 750 positive, no zeros). Outcome vote: Democratic vote share at t+2 for the same seat (93 missing, so N = 1,297 in H1). Covariates: class, termshouse, termssenate, population. termshouse and termssenate are missing for the same 282 rows. Sample restrictions: none beyond rdrobust's removal of missing outcomes; no bandwidth window is imposed beyond the bandwidths the estimator selects. Design checks already run (dr-checks, no vote statistic): the file matches the printed CCFT 2017 Sec. 7.2 moments and counts for non-outcome variables and counts (32 comparisons; vote's moments were not compared). Ties in margin occur only at +/-100, none within |margin| <= 30. Raw data are not committed.
analysis_plan: 1. design-mde (kind data-prep, code/design_mde.py, run id design-mde, runs/design-mde/metrics.json): margin and covariates only; vote is never loaded (outcome_loaded = 0). Logs the H2(a) density MDE (0.01136), the H2(b) covariate MDEs (class 0.401, termshouse 1.400, termssenate 2.091, population 2,185,253) and the margin-only density statistic (T_Q -0.875, p 0.381). Completed before any analysis run. Pre-gate estimation, disclosed.

2. h1-rdrobust (kind analysis, code/h1_replication.py): main specification with masspoints = 'off' (primary) and the same run with masspoints = 'adjust' (secondary). Metrics per setting: conv_coef, conv_se, ci_low, ci_high (robust), h, b, N, N_left, N_right, M_left, M_right. Claims: rd-effect (conv_coef), rd-ci-low (ci_low), rd-ci-high (ci_high), rd-n (N), rd-bw (h), all from the 'off' setting. Tolerance verdict on 'off' only; failure reported as failure.

3. h2-density (kind analysis, code/h2_density.py): rddensity on margin, N = 1,390. Metrics: T_conv, p_conv, T_Q, p_Q, bandwidth, n_left, n_right, and the sensitivity p_Q_nomass (massPoints = False). Claim: rd-density-p (p_Q). Reproduces the design-mde specification (p = 0.381). Single test, no correction.

4. h2-covariates (kind analysis, code/h2_covariates.py): four rdrobust runs with the H1 options at masspoints = 'off'. Metrics per covariate: coef, se, ci_low, ci_high, p_robust, N, h, N_h left and right, bw_capped, MDE, plus Holm-adjusted p within this family. Claims: rd-cov-class-p, rd-cov-termshouse-p, rd-cov-termssenate-p, rd-cov-population-p (compared with the printed 0.897, 0.561, 0.901, 0.634 in CCFT 2017 Sec. 7.4, same four covariates).

5. h2-placebo (kind analysis, code/h2_placebo.py): two one-sided rdrobust runs at c_L and c_R on vote, report-only. Metrics per side: coef, se, ci_low, ci_high, p_robust, N, h, b, N_h left and right, bw_max (one-sided sample, rdbwselect.py lines 651-655), bw_capped (h or b equals bw_max), sd_vote_side (descriptive). Claims: rd-placebo-left-est, rd-placebo-right-est, with CI width as the precision statement.

6. h2-selection (kind analysis, code/h2_selection.py, run after the design gate only): rdrobust(y = vote_observed, x = margin) on all 1,390 rows with the H1 options at masspoints = 'off'. Metrics: coef, se, ci_low, ci_high, p_robust, N, h, MDE computed from se. Claim: rd-selection-p (p_robust). Single test, no correction.

7. h3-sensitivity (kind analysis, code/h3_sensitivity.py): five specifications in the H3 list, reported as one table next to H1; no decision rule. Claims: rd-h3-2014-bw-effect, rd-h3-half-bw-effect, rd-h3-double-bw-effect, rd-h3-p2-effect, rd-h3-adjust-effect.
8. Clean rerun (crew.py rerun) after all runs, against the ledger, to confirm H1 and H2 reproduce. No new estimates.
threats: Software: the printed numbers come from the 2016 release, not rdrobust 2.1.1. H1 may fail for reasons not in the design; a failure under 'off' is reported as a failure and diagnosed by version, platform and option, not tuned. H1 is a computational check and is not evidence about the incumbency advantage (run h1-rdrobust; H3 rows).

Mass points: 'off' is an assumption about the 2016 release, not a sourced fact. Under 'adjust' the bandwidth selector uses M (1,352 distinct margin values) in place of N, so h changes even though the bwcheck trigger (20 percent mass share on a side) is not met. Both settings are reported in the same run (run h1-rdrobust; H3 row v).

Data fidelity: the CSV comes from the rdrobust repository, not from the .dta used by CCFT. The dr-checks run matches the printed non-outcome moments and counts, but not vote's moments, which were not compared before the gate. H1 is the first outcome check. The codebook wording is for the Data RA to narrow (review F5).
Covariate set: only four of the eight covariates of CFT 2015 are in the file. The H2(b) tests are not compared one-to-one with CFT 2015 (run h2-covariates).

Non-rejection is weak evidence: density and covariate tests at N = 1,390 may have low power, so the stated MDEs are reported next to every null result (runs design-mde, h2-density, h2-covariates). H2(c) is report-only and makes no non-rejection claim.

Multiplicity: each family is corrected on its own and no cross-family conclusion is drawn. H2(b) is Holm over four covariates. H2(a), H2(c) and H2(d) are single tests reported without correction. H2(c) has no conclusion attached.
Selection into the outcome: 93 elections have no vote. A discontinuity in vote_observed at the cutoff would bias H1. Tested by H2(d) (run h2-selection, after the gate), with its MDE fixed now.

Placebo windows: each one-sided placebo sample has its own bandwidth cap, bw_max = max(|c - x_min|, |c - x_max|) over that sample (not |c|). A placebo whose final h or b equals bw_max is flagged bw_capped = 1 and reported as boundary-limited, with bw_max, h, b and N_h on each side recorded (run h2-placebo).

Local estimand: the estimate is local to close elections (bandwidth about 17.7 points). The paper must not call it the incumbency advantage in all elections, as the seed requires. State-clustered inference (CCFT 2017 Sec. 7.4) is not in this plan; it is disclosed rather than added after seeing results.

Pre-gate estimation: design-mde recorded the margin-only density statistic (p = 0.381) and the covariate SEs before the design gate. Both are disclosed; the analysis runs repeat them with the same settings (PI decision, review F4).

Placebo bound (H2c): the bound from the original design is withdrawn. H2(c) is report-only, so no equivalence bound is stated and none is needed for the conclusion. The chosen-constant issue no longer applies.

tasks.title: The published estimate (CCFT 2017, Stata Journal 17(2); data of Cattaneo, Frandsen and Titiunik 2015), its exact specification and software version; prior replications and the falsification checks used in that literature

Run fetch-data (data-prep): download rdrobust_senate.csv from the seed URL, verify sha256, record in data/manifest.json with source, licence note, date and hash; prepare-data: data/CODEBOOK.md with variables, N, missingness and ranges of margin and covariates; no statistic of vote by side of the cutoff

Design-stage data checks (data-prep, no vote statistic): ties and mass points in margin; compare the CSV's printed moments for margin, class and population with CCFT 2017 Sec. 7.2 (or other printed descriptive statistics) to establish that the file matches the one used; report in data/CODEBOOK.md
Run design-mde (data-prep, margin and covariate counts only, code/design_mde.py): rddensity null SE and placebo cutoffs c_L, c_R; before any analysis run
Run h1-rdrobust (code/h1_replication.py): main rdrobust specification, pinned 2.1.1, masspoints off; check tolerances; rd-effect, rd-ci-low, rd-ci-high, rd-n, rd-bw
Run h2-density (code/h2_density.py): rddensity on margin, N = 1,390; robust p-value and MDE from design-mde
Run h2-covariates (code/h2_covariates.py): four covariate rdrobust tests with H1 options, N = 1,390 or 1,108, Holm, MDE per test
Run h2-placebo (code/h2_placebo.py): one-sided placebo cutoffs c_L and c_R on vote, report-only (estimate, CI, N, bandwidth, bw_capped)
Run h3-sensitivity (code/h3_sensitivity.py): five descriptive specifications next to H1; no decision rule
Write claims.jsonl entries for every reported number, each linked to its run (rd-effect, rd-ci-low, rd-ci-high and the rest of the design list)
Clean rerun (crew.py rerun) after all runs; confirm metrics match the ledger
Run h2-selection (code/h2_selection.py) after the design gate: rdrobust on vote_observed with H1 options; MDE computed here, not before the gate

disclosures: 2026-11-20 (question stage, PI): By the human's choice this workspace is a low-cost trial. Every role subagent, including the Reviewer, runs on Claude Haiku 5.5; the PI session runs on Claude Opus 5.5. Cost is measured with crew/scripts/usage.py and compared with the other gallery papers.

2026-11-20 (design stage, PI ruling on design-r1 F4): design-mde, logged as a data-prep run before the design gate, ran rddensity on margin (the H2(a) test itself: T_Q = -0.875, p = 0.381) and rdrobust with each of the four covariates as outcome to obtain the standard errors used for the H2(b) MDEs. No vote value was loaded. These are falsification-test computations seen before the gate. The PI accepts them with this disclosure: the H2(a) and H2(b) analysis runs after the gate repeat them with the same settings, and the paper reports that the H2(a) result and the H2(b) standard errors were seen at the design stage.
